design_summary.purpose: adaptive_aero_control_top is the required synthesizable FPGA top for a compact adaptive aero control controller around an externally executed physics surrogate. It provides a 64-bit MMIO control/status plane, packages bounded surrogate requests, validates bounded surrogate responses, monitors timeout and staleness, selects safe fallback behavior, registers actuator outputs, and generates interrupt/status indication.
design_summary.operating_model: The top operates synchronously on clk with active-low rst_n. Firmware configures compact control registers, launches a surrogate request, and the RTL holds surrogate_req_valid until surrogate_req_ready is observed. The external service returns surrogate_rsp_valid/surrogate_rsp_data, which the RTL accepts through surrogate_rsp_ready, validates against sequence/token, freshness, timeout, and range rules, then clamps and optionally step-limits the suggested actuator command before passing it to a registered output stage. Any disable, reset, timeout, stale, protocol, malformed, or out-of-range condition drives deterministic safe fallback. The design remains agnostic to raw geometry payloads and only transports compact identifiers and operating metadata.

external_interfaces.name: MMIO register window
external_interfaces.intent: Compact 64-bit memory-mapped configuration and telemetry access for control enable, launch, faults, timeout thresholds, limits, fallback, sequence control, and status readback.

external_interfaces.name: Surrogate request transport
external_interfaces.intent: Outbound valid/data are driven by RTL and ready is received from the external surrogate service, with one outstanding transaction held until accepted unless limited pipelining is enabled.

external_interfaces.name: Surrogate response transport
external_interfaces.intent: Inbound valid/data are received from the external surrogate service and ready is driven by RTL to accept validated responses without combinational dependence on the request path.

external_interfaces.name: Actuator interface
external_interfaces.intent: Registered bounded actuator command output with validity and mode encoding for normal update, fallback hold, or fault-safe state.

external_interfaces.name: Status interrupt
external_interfaces.intent: Synchronous interrupt/status indication for response acceptance, timeout, or fault entry according to configuration.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_regfile
module_architecture.role: Compact MMIO register file and decode block for control, status, timeout, limits, fallback, operating-point metadata, request sequencing, and interrupt configuration.
responsibilities: Decode MMIO reads and writes into semantic configuration fields.
Provide deterministic reset values and write masking via mmio_wstrb.
Expose status and telemetry readback to firmware.
Support control of launch, enable, fault clear, sticky-fault retention, and session rollover behavior.
Provide compact operating-point fields sufficient for 20 to 55 m/s envelope and the representative 38.89 m/s operating point.
Return mmio_error for unsupported addresses or invalid accesses.
Hold configuration stable until rewritten by firmware.
interface_notes: Drives semantic control outputs consumed by downstream controller blocks; it does not drive transport or actuator outputs directly.
Receives telemetry inputs for status readback only.

The register map includes control enable, soft reset, launch, fault clear, sticky fault, pipelined mode, outstanding limit, timeout/freshness thresholds, min/max/fallback/step-limit command fields, IRQ policy bits, request type, sequence seed, operating velocity, velocity fraction, reference ID, geometry ID, session rollover, and status clear.
Unsupported or malformed accesses are reported through mmio_error while legal accesses return mmio_rdata and mmio_rvalid.
ownership_notes: Owns the semantic configuration plane and MMIO-facing outputs.
Does not own telemetry inputs, transport handshakes, or actuator outputs.
rtl_output_file: adaptive_aero_control_regfile.v

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_request_packager
module_architecture.role: Outbound surrogate request constructor and launch sequencer.
responsibilities: Form outbound request payloads from semantic configuration fields.
Manage one-at-a-time request issue by default, or limited pipelined issuance when configured.
Hold request valid until ready handshake completes.
Generate the active sequence number for validation and timeout tracking.
Assert request issuance only when enabled and launch is requested.
Provide a clean boundary between register semantics and transport payload encoding.
interface_notes: Emits surrogate_req_valid and surrogate_req_data as top-level outputs; surrogate_req_ready is received as an input from the external service per the mandatory transport direction contract.
Includes monotonically incrementing sequence numbering, request type tagging, compact operating-point metadata, and compact model identifiers in the 64-bit request word.
req_launch_accepted marks a request accepted into the outstanding set, req_seq_active identifies the active sequence, and req_outstanding_inc supports outstanding-count tracking.
Request issuance is inhibited when disabled or when the configured outstanding limit is reached.
ownership_notes: Owns request transport generation and request-issue acceptance signaling.
Does not own response validation, fallback selection, or actuator staging.
rtl_output_file: adaptive_aero_request_packager.v

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_response_validator
module_architecture.role: Inbound surrogate response acceptance, validation, and bounded command suggestion checker.
responsibilities: Assert surrogate response readiness when able to accept a response.
Parse response data into sequence/token and actuator suggestion fields.
Validate sequence match, freshness, and timeout status.
Classify protocol, timeout, and stale faults separately.
Clamp accepted actuator suggestions to configured bounds and report clamp activity.
Provide accepted command and response acceptance count to controller and telemetry.
Ensure stale-data conditions are reported when session rollover or request age rules indicate stale data.
interface_notes: Receives surrogate_rsp_valid and surrogate_rsp_data as inputs from the external service and drives surrogate_rsp_ready as an RTL output, consistent with the mandatory transport direction contract.
Accepts only valid, sequence-matched, fresh, and non-timed-out responses; rejected responses do not update command state.
rsp_accepted_cmd is a bounded semantic command suggestion, not the final actuator output.
Range checking and optional step limiting occur before downstream use.
The validator remains free of combinational loops with the request packager and controller.
ownership_notes: Owns response acceptance strobes, fault classification outputs, bounded accepted command suggestion, and response counter.
Does not own the final actuator outputs or fallback policy.
rtl_output_file: adaptive_aero_response_validator.v

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_timeout_monitor
module_architecture.role: Request age, outstanding-count, timeout, and stale-data monitor.
responsibilities: Track request age for the active request or limited outstanding set.
Assert timeout_expired when configured threshold is exceeded.
Assert stale_session_event when freshness or rollover conditions indicate stale data.
Provide busy and outstanding_count status for telemetry and gating.
Latch timeout fault state until cleared per control policy.
Remain synchronous and bounded to small counter logic only.
interface_notes: Consumes request-launch acceptance and response-accept strobes to update age and outstanding tracking.
Outputs request_age, outstanding_count, busy, timeout_expired, stale_session_event, and timeout_fault_latched for controller, validator, and telemetry use.
Works for either single-current-request or limited pipelined operation within the configured outstanding limit.
The monitor does not inspect response payload contents to advance age.
ownership_notes: Owns timeout and freshness counters plus latched timeout fault indication.
Does not own MMIO configuration or any transport port.
rtl_output_file: adaptive_aero_timeout_monitor.v

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_fallback_controller
module_architecture.role: Deterministic safe-command selector and fault-state manager.
responsibilities: Choose safe fallback command whenever the system is disabled, in reset, or any fault is present.
Hold a deterministic fallback command stable until explicit clear or accepted new command policy allows change.
Propagate fault classification bits for timeout, stale, and protocol failure.
Forward only bounded and optionally step-limited command suggestions to the actuator stage.
Respect sticky-fault retention behavior when configured.
Provide a safe command that is conservative for aero control and valid across the supported envelope.
interface_notes: Consumes validated command suggestions and fault indicators from the response validator plus timeout-latched status from the monitor.
Outputs safe_cmd, fallback_active, fault_active, clamp_active, and the fault classification bits used for telemetry and output staging.
cfg_fault_clear and cfg_sticky_fault govern release and retention of fault states.
The controller never emits an unclamped command; clamp activity reflects any min/max or step-limit correction.
ownership_notes: Owns fallback selection semantics and fault consolidation before the registered actuator stage.
Does not own the actuator output pins themselves.
rtl_output_file: adaptive_aero_fallback_controller.v

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_actuator_output_stage
module_architecture.role: Registered actuator output pipeline and mode encoder.
responsibilities: Register the final command and valid indication.
Encode actuator_mode according to normal, fallback, and fault-safe behavior.
Ensure output is stable across cycles when no new update occurs.
Provide a registered update pulse when a command is accepted or fallback state changes.
Never emit an unclamped or unbounded actuator command.
interface_notes: Drives actuator_cmd, actuator_valid, and actuator_mode as top-level outputs.
Consumes the controller-selected safe_cmd and fallback/fault indicators; the registered output is the only source of top-level actuator command emission.
The stage guarantees bounded output and preserves command stability across cycles.
Update pulses are internal telemetry aids and do not create combinational feedback.
ownership_notes: Owns the final actuator output registration and mode encoding.
Does not own command selection logic or fault decisions.
rtl_output_file: adaptive_aero_actuator_output_stage.v

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_telemetry_status
module_architecture.role: Telemetry aggregation and IRQ generation block.
responsibilities: Provide status IRQ behavior tied to acceptance, timeout, and fault events.
Aggregate telemetry fields for readback by the register file.
Maintain deterministic IRQ clear behavior under cfg_status_clear and reset.
Ensure all telemetry signals are synchronized and stable for MMIO readout.
Expose current state machine state and health indicators without modifying them.
interface_notes: Consumes telemetry_state, telemetry_busy, telemetry_outstanding_count, telemetry_last_seq, timeout/stale/protocol/clamp/fallback indicators, response counter, and IRQ latch state.
Drives status_irq as the sole top-level interrupt/status output.
IRQ behavior is configured by cfg_irq_on_accept, cfg_irq_on_fault, and cfg_irq_on_timeout with synchronous clear via cfg_status_clear.
Telemetry is read-only aggregation; it does not alter controller state.
ownership_notes: Owns the IRQ output behavior and telemetry aggregation path.
Does not own raw control settings or transport handshakes.
rtl_output_file: adaptive_aero_telemetry_status.v

interface_summary.intent: Provide compact semantic launch, sequencing, operating-point, and model-identifier metadata for outbound request construction.
Provide validation, range-limit, and freshness configuration for inbound response checking.
Configure age tracking, timeout detection, stale detection, and limited pipelining bookkeeping.
Configure fallback selection, fault retention, and bounded-command policy.
Configure IRQ behavior and status clear policy.
Notify the monitor when a request has been accepted into the outstanding set so age and busy tracking can begin.
Provide the active request sequence context used to validate inbound responses.
Provide the freshness, timeout, and stale-data indicators used to accept or reject a response.
Provide latched timeout status to force safe fallback until cleared per policy.
Pass accepted bounded command suggestions and fault classifications into the fallback controller.
Provide the deterministic safe command and state qualifiers for the final registered actuator output.
Allow the monitor to decrement outstanding tracking when a valid response is accepted.
Provide a registered update event so the output stage can qualify a new actuator update pulse when a response is accepted.
Supply response-count and acceptance/clamp information for status reporting.
Provide response health and clamp status for readback aggregation.
Provide fallback and fault-state indicators for telemetry.
Expose registered actuator output state for telemetry where internally aggregated.

data_flow_summary: Firmware programs compact MMIO registers in adaptive_aero_control_regfile, including enable, launch, timeout, freshness, min/max/fallback/step limits, sequencing, and operating-point metadata.

adaptive_aero_request_packager creates a single bounded 64-bit surrogate request per accepted launch, embeds the next sequence number plus request type and compact operating-point/model identifiers, and holds surrogate_req_valid until surrogate_req_ready is observed.
adaptive_aero_timeout_monitor tracks request age, busy state, outstanding count, timeout expiration, and stale-session detection, feeding both validation and fallback logic.

adaptive_aero_response_validator accepts surrogate_rsp_valid/surrogate_rsp_data only when sequence, freshness, timeout, and range conditions are satisfied; otherwise it classifies protocol, timeout, or stale faults and prevents command update.
When a response is accepted, the validator emits a bounded command suggestion that may still be clamped or step-limited before it is used by fallback control.

adaptive_aero_fallback_controller selects between the bounded accepted command and deterministic safe fallback based on enable, reset, fault, timeout, sticky-fault, and fault-clear policy, while retaining conservative safe behavior when required.
adaptive_aero_actuator_output_stage registers the final bounded command, valid, and mode outputs so that no top-level actuator pin is driven by an unclamped or combinationally generated value.
adaptive_aero_telemetry_status aggregates controller health and state into telemetry and generates status_irq according to configuration and event type.

No bulk geometry or payload storage is represented as register flattening; compact identifiers and metadata only are transported in RTL, and any deeper queueing or storage requirement remains technology-neutral and FPGA-mappable to native block RAM if later needed.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: All logic is fully synchronous to clk. The top-level design and all child modules use clk as the sole clock domain described in the spec, with no combinational loop permitted between request and response handshakes.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: rst_n is active-low. On deassertion/reset assertion, the design clears outstanding requests, clears request and response valid outputs, initializes actuator_cmd to the fallback or conservative default, asserts fallback active, clears fault latches unless sticky-fault retention is configured, sets the module idle, and initializes counters and sequence tracking deterministically. The telemetry IRQ is deasserted on reset unless a configured retention policy exists outside the normal path.

integration_notes: The top module adaptive_aero_control_top is the required design top and must not be substituted by any status, telemetry, register-bank, or leaf module.

The external model transport direction is fixed by contract: the RTL drives surrogate_req_valid and surrogate_req_data and receives surrogate_req_ready; the RTL receives surrogate_rsp_valid and surrogate_rsp_data and drives surrogate_rsp_ready.
A required top-level output must always have a real RTL driver at the top level; no required output may rely only on a child input connection.
The design is strictly descriptive here; no hierarchy, port names, or filenames are altered from the specification.

The architecture is suitable for an Arch2RTL-style FPGA implementation that surrounds an externally executed physics surrogate with validation, bounded I/O, safety, timeout, stale-data handling, fallback, and deterministic actuator command behavior.

FPGA memory usage, if needed for future queueing or history, should be expressed through technology-neutral wrapper storage that the FPGA flow can map to block RAM; the current compact control plane does not flatten bulk storage into registers.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
